board_events.text: Step 2: from the balanced equation, 1 mol dichromate oxidises 6 mol Fe$^{2+}$.
Cross-check by equivalents: $0.49/49=0.01$ eq $=0.01$ mol Fe$^{2+}$ (its $n=1$).
The n-factor 6 does all the work — fix it first, then it is one multiplication.

segments.text: Now a J E E Main numerical that rewards fixing the n-factor first. We dissolve zero point four nine grams of pure potassium dichromate in dilute sulphuric acid and use it to oxidise iron two ions completely; how many moles of iron two are oxidised?
Step one, moles of dichromate. Zero point four nine grams divided by the molar mass two hundred ninety four gives one point six seven times ten to the minus three moles.
The board shows the stoichiometry that does the heavy lifting.

Step two, the ratio. From the balanced equation we derived earlier, one mole of dichromate oxidises six moles of iron two, because the dichromate n-factor is six and each iron two donates one electron.
So multiply: one point six seven times ten to the minus three, times six, gives one point zero times ten to the minus two moles of iron two.

Cross-check by the equivalents route, which should always agree. Equivalents of dichromate are zero point four nine over forty nine, that is zero point zero one equivalents, and since iron two has an n-factor of one, that equals zero point zero one moles. Consistent.
Notice the whole problem turned on the n-factor of six. Fix that first, and the numerical is a single multiplication rather than a balancing exercise under time pressure.

अब एक J E E Main numerical जो n-factor पहले fix करने पर reward देता है। हम zero point four nine grams pure potassium dichromate को dilute sulphuric acid में घोलकर iron two ions को पूरी तरह oxidise करते हैं; कितने moles iron two oxidise होते हैं?
Step one, dichromate के moles। Zero point four nine grams को molar mass two hundred ninety four से भाग देने पर one point six seven times ten to the minus three moles मिलते हैं।
Board वो stoichiometry दिखाता है जो असली काम करती है।
Step two, ratio। पहले derive की balanced equation से, एक mole dichromate छह moles iron two oxidise करता है, क्योंकि dichromate n-factor six है और हर iron two एक electron देता है।
तो multiply करो: one point six seven times ten to the minus three, times छह, देता है one point zero times ten to the minus two moles iron two।

Equivalents route से cross-check करो, जो हमेशा agree करना चाहिए। Dichromate के equivalents हैं zero point four nine over forty nine, यानी zero point zero one equivalents, और iron two का n-factor one होने से ये zero point zero one moles के बराबर है। Consistent।
ध्यान दो पूरा problem n-factor छह पर घूमा। उसे पहले fix करो, और numerical time pressure में balancing exercise नहीं बल्कि एक multiplication रह जाता है।

board_events.text: Acidic: Mn falls to Mn$^{2+}$ ($n=5$); iodide is oxidised only as far as $\text{I}_2$.
Neutral / faintly alkaline: Mn stops at MnO$_2$ ($n=3$); iodide is driven to iodate.
The medium controls BOTH the Mn product AND how far the reductant is oxidised.

segments.text: This J E E Advanced question drives home the deepest idea of the subtopic: in permanganate chemistry the medium controls not just the manganese product but how far the other reactant is pushed. We write both equations for permanganate reacting with potassium iodide.
The board contrasts the two media side by side.

In acidic medium the manganese half is the five-electron one, falling to manganese two. Here iodide is oxidised only as far as molecular iodine: two permanganate plus ten iodide plus sixteen protons give two manganese two, five iodine molecules, and eight waters.
So under strong acid, the fast, high-potential reaction stops iodide at iodine before it can go further.
In neutral or faintly alkaline medium the manganese half is the three-electron one, stopping at manganese dioxide. And now, strikingly, the iodide is driven all the way to iodate.
That second equation: two permanganate plus water plus iodide give two manganese dioxide, two hydroxide, and the iodate ion.

Why the difference? The gentler, more prolonged oxidation at the surface of the forming manganese dioxide, in alkaline conditions that disfavour molecular iodine, pushes iodine on to the fully oxidised iodate. The lesson to carry away: the medium sets both the manganese product and the depth of the reductant's oxidation.

ये J E E Advanced question subtopic का सबसे गहरा idea पक्का करता है: permanganate chemistry में medium सिर्फ manganese product नहीं बल्कि ये भी तय करता है कि दूसरा reactant कितना दूर धकेला जाता है। हम permanganate की potassium iodide के साथ दोनों equations लिखते हैं।
Board दोनों media को side by side contrast करता है।

Acidic medium में manganese half पाँच-electron वाला है, manganese two तक गिरता है। यहाँ iodide सिर्फ molecular iodine तक oxidise होता है: दो permanganate plus दस iodide plus सोलह protons देते हैं दो manganese two, पाँच iodine molecules, और आठ waters।
तो strong acid में fast, high-potential reaction iodide को iodine पर रोक देती है, आगे जाने से पहले।
Neutral या faintly alkaline medium में manganese half तीन-electron वाला है, manganese dioxide पर रुकता है। और अब, हैरानी से, iodide पूरा iodate तक धकेला जाता है।
वो दूसरी equation: दो permanganate plus water plus iodide देते हैं दो manganese dioxide, दो hydroxide, और iodate ion।

फ़र्क़ क्यों? बनते manganese dioxide की surface पर gentler, ज़्यादा देर चलने वाली oxidation, alkaline conditions में जो molecular iodine को disfavour करती हैं, iodine को आगे fully oxidised iodate तक धकेलती है। साथ ले जाने का lesson: medium manganese product और reductant की oxidation की depth दोनों तय करता है।

board_events.text: Four traps that drain marks on this high-yield topic
Trap 1: acidifying KMnO$_4$ with HCl. Always dilute H$_2$SO$_4$ — HCl is oxidised to Cl$_2$.
Trap 2: one fixed permanganate product. The Mn product depends on medium — apply 5–3–1 each time.
Trap 3: calling the purple/orange colour a $d$–$d$ transition. Both centres are $d^0$ — it is L M C T.
Trap 4: wrong n-factor. Dichromate is 6; permanganate is 5 / 3 / 1 by medium.

board_events.caption: Exam-hall reference card

<rect x="240" y="40" width="200" height="60" fill="#fef3c7" stroke="#1e293b"/>

board_events.text: Mnemonics: '5-3-1 = Acid-Neutral-Base'; 'acid $\rightarrow$ orange, base $\rightarrow$ yellow'.

segments.text: Let us close this high-yield subtopic with the four traps that quietly drain marks, and the two mnemonics that lock the essentials.

Trap one, the deadliest in the lab. Never acidify permanganate with hydrochloric acid; always use dilute sulphuric acid, because hydrochloric acid is oxidised to chlorine and ruins any quantitative result.
Trap two, writing one fixed permanganate product. The manganese product depends on the medium, so apply the five-three-one rule every single time rather than defaulting to manganese two.

Trap three, over-applying last subtopic's colour rule. The intense purple of permanganate and orange of dichromate are not d to d transitions, both metal centres are d-zero, so the colour is a ligand-to-metal charge transfer, L M C T.

Trap four, the single biggest source of lost marks in volumetric numericals, using the wrong n-factor. Dichromate is six; permanganate is five in acid, three in neutral, one in alkali. Mixing these wrecks the equivalent-mass answer.
Keep the reference card on the board in your head.

And lock in two mnemonics. For the electron counts, five-three-one equals acid-neutral-base, a strong to weak grip on electrons. For the dichromate colour, acid gives orange and base gives yellow. Fix the n-factor first, and most of this subtopic's numericals fall out in one line.
इस high-yield subtopic को चार traps के साथ बंद करते हैं जो चुपचाप marks खाते हैं, और दो mnemonics जो essentials lock करते हैं।

Trap one, lab में सबसे ख़तरनाक। Permanganate को कभी hydrochloric acid से acidify मत करो; हमेशा dilute sulphuric acid use करो, क्योंकि hydrochloric acid chlorine में oxidise होकर quantitative result बर्बाद कर देता है।
Trap two, एक fixed permanganate product लिखना। Manganese product medium पर निर्भर करता है, तो manganese two पर default करने के बजाय हर बार five-three-one rule लगाओ।

Trap three, पिछले subtopic का colour rule over-apply करना। Permanganate का intense purple और dichromate का orange d to d transitions नहीं हैं, दोनों metal centres d-zero हैं, तो colour एक ligand-to-metal charge transfer है, L M C T।

Trap four, volumetric numericals में सबसे बड़ा marks-loss का source, ग़लत n-factor use करना। Dichromate six है; permanganate acid में five, neutral में three, alkali में one। इन्हें मिलाना equivalent-mass answer बिगाड़ देता है।
Board का reference card दिमाग़ में रखो।

और दो mnemonics lock करो। Electron counts के लिए, five-three-one equals acid-neutral-base, electrons पर strong to weak grip। Dichromate colour के लिए, acid देता है orange और base देता है yellow। n-factor पहले fix करो, और इस subtopic के ज़्यादातर numericals एक line में निकल आते हैं।

board_events.text: Pulling all fourteen of each in-line would stretch the table absurdly — it is drawing convenience.
Their newest electron enters the $(n-2)f$ orbitals: $4f$ for lanthanoids, $5f$ for actinoids.
Those $f$-electrons are buried deep, shielded by outer shells, so they barely touch chemistry.
Hence all fourteen lanthanoids behave almost identically — overwhelmingly $+3$ and hard to separate.
So alike that they are often used as a ready-made mixture, mischmetall, rather than pure metals.

segments.text: <curious>Ever wondered about those two lonely rows floating below the periodic table, as if torn off and pinned at the bottom?</curious> Those are the f-block, the lanthanoids and the actinoids.
They are not really exiles. As the board shows, they genuinely belong in group three, periods six and seven, sitting right after lanthanum and actinium.

So why the footnote panel? Because slotting all fourteen of each in-line would stretch the table absurdly wide, like fitting an entire wedding baraat through a single doorway. It is purely a matter of drawing convenience.

What truly defines them is where the newest electron goes. Not the penultimate shell as in the d-block, but one level deeper, into the n-minus-two f orbitals: four f for the lanthanoids, five f for the actinoids.
Picture a bank vault. Electrons locked that deep are shielded by the outer shells sitting above them, so they barely take part in chemistry at all.

This single fact explains the family's personality. All fourteen lanthanoids behave almost identically, overwhelmingly showing the plus three state, and they are notoriously hard to separate from one another.

They are so chemically alike that for most industrial purposes we do not separate them at all. We use them as a ready-made mixture, which is exactly why a blended alloy like mischmetall is far cheaper and more common than any single pure rare-earth metal.
<curious>कभी सोचा है periodic table के नीचे तैरती उन दो अकेली rows के बारे में, जैसे किसी ने फाड़कर नीचे pin कर दी हों?</curious> वो हैं f-block, lanthanoids और actinoids।
ये असल में exiles नहीं हैं। जैसे board दिखाता है, ये सचमुच group three, periods six और seven में हैं, lanthanum और actinium के ठीक बाद।
तो footnote panel क्यों? क्योंकि हर एक के चौदह elements in-line डालने से table बेतुकी चौड़ी हो जाती, जैसे पूरी शादी की baraat एक दरवाज़े से निकालना। ये बस drawing convenience है।

इन्हें असल में define करता है नया electron कहाँ जाता है। d-block की तरह penultimate shell में नहीं, बल्कि एक level और गहरे, n-minus-two f orbitals में: lanthanoids के लिए four f, actinoids के लिए five f।
एक bank vault सोचो। इतने गहरे locked electrons ऊपर बैठी outer shells से shielded होते हैं, तो ये chemistry में मुश्किल से हिस्सा लेते हैं।
यही एक बात family की personality समझा देती है। चौदहों lanthanoids लगभग एक जैसे behave करते हैं, ज़्यादातर plus three state दिखाते हैं, और एक-दूसरे से अलग करना बेहद मुश्किल है।

ये इतने chemically alike हैं कि ज़्यादातर industrial कामों के लिए हम इन्हें अलग करते ही नहीं। इन्हें ready-made mixture की तरह इस्तेमाल करते हैं, यही वजह है कि mischmetall जैसा blended alloy किसी भी single pure rare-earth metal से सस्ता और आम है।

board_events.text: Lanthanoids run Ce ($Z=58$) to Lu ($Z=71$); actinoids Th ($Z=90$) to Lr ($Z=103$).
La ($Z=57$) and Ac ($Z=89$) are formally $d$-block, studied here by resemblance.
Anomalies trace to the stability of empty $f^0$, half-filled $f^7$ and full $f^{14}$ subshells.

segments.text: Let us fix the electronic bookkeeping, because every property in this subtopic falls out of it. The general configuration is on the board.
Read it as n-minus-two f, holding one to fourteen electrons, then n-minus-one d holding zero or one, and finally the outer n s two.
The template, the plus three rule, and the famous anomaly are all in the diagram.
The lanthanoids run from cerium, atomic number fifty eight, to lutetium, seventy one. The actinoids run from thorium, ninety, to lawrencium, one hundred three.

A common exam catch: lanthanum, fifty seven, and actinium, eighty nine, are formally d-block elements, because their differentiating electron is in d, not f. We study them here only by close resemblance.

The workhorse rule is that the most stable ion, plus three, gives the clean series lanthanoid three plus equals four f to the n. But watch gadolinium: it is xenon core, four f seven, five d one, six s two.

Why the extra electron sits in five d rather than pairing into four f is the whole theme of this subtopic. The empty, half-filled and fully-filled f subshells, f-zero, f-seven and f-fourteen, are unusually stable. Those three stability magnets will explain the anomalies, the colours, the magnetism and the odd oxidation states, all from one idea.
Electronic bookkeeping fix कर लेते हैं, क्योंकि इस subtopic की हर property इसी से निकलती है। General configuration board पर है।
इसे पढ़ो n-minus-two f, जिसमें एक से चौदह electrons, फिर n-minus-one d जिसमें zero या one, और आख़िर में outer n s two।
Template, plus three rule, और मशहूर anomaly सब diagram में हैं।
Lanthanoids चलते हैं cerium, atomic number fifty eight, से lutetium, seventy one तक। Actinoids चलते हैं thorium, ninety, से lawrencium, one hundred three तक।

एक common exam catch: lanthanum, fifty seven, और actinium, eighty nine, formally d-block elements हैं, क्योंकि इनका differentiating electron d में है, f में नहीं। हम इन्हें यहाँ सिर्फ close resemblance से पढ़ते हैं।
Workhorse rule ये है कि सबसे stable ion, plus three, clean series देता है, lanthanoid three plus equals four f to the n। पर gadolinium देखो: ये xenon core, four f seven, five d one, six s two है।

Extra electron five d में क्यों बैठता है, four f में pair होने के बजाय, यही इस subtopic की पूरी theme है। Empty, half-filled और fully-filled f subshells, f-zero, f-seven और f-fourteen, असामान्य रूप से stable हैं। वो तीन stability magnets anomalies, colours, magnetism और अजीब oxidation states, सब एक idea से समझा देंगे।

board_events.text: Each added $4f$ electron shields the nucleus poorly — the $f$ orbitals are diffuse and inner.
So effective nuclear charge creeps up across the series, pulling the cloud inward.
The decrease is perfectly regular for the $\text{Ln}^{3+}$ ions, only roughly so for the atoms.
The pay-off shows one row below: Zr and Hf end up at $160$ and $159$ pm — almost identical.
Historically misnamed 'rare earths'; only promethium is genuinely scarce (radioactive, artificial).

segments.text: Now the single most examined idea in the whole f-block: the lanthanoid contraction. It has a lovely, intuitive cause.
The board plots it: the ionic radius falls steadily and smoothly as we move from lanthanum to lutetium.
Here is the mechanism. Imagine the fourteen four f electrons boarding one at a time. Each new electron is a poor bodyguard, an f electron shields the others from the nucleus very ineffectively.

So with every boarding, the rising nuclear charge, like a conductor tightening his grip, pulls the whole electron cloud inward a little more. Each tug is tiny, but across fourteen elements it accumulates into a steady shrinkage.
One precision point examiners reward: the decrease is perfectly regular for the lanthanoid three plus ions, and only roughly regular for the neutral atoms.

The dramatic pay-off shows up one row below in the periodic table. The contraction almost exactly cancels the size increase expected for the third transition series, so zirconium and hafnium end up at one hundred sixty and one hundred fifty nine picometres, virtually identical.

One naming footnote: the lanthanoids were misleadingly called the rare earths, although most are not rare at all. Only promethium is genuinely scarce, existing only as an artificial radioactive element.
अब पूरे f-block का सबसे ज़्यादा पूछा जाने वाला idea: lanthanoid contraction। इसकी वजह बहुत ख़ूबसूरत और intuitive है।
Board इसे plot करता है: ionic radius steadily और smoothly गिरता है जैसे-जैसे हम lanthanum से lutetium की ओर बढ़ते हैं।
ये रहा mechanism। सोचो चौदह four f electrons एक-एक करके board कर रहे हैं। हर नया electron एक poor bodyguard है, एक f electron बाक़ियों को nucleus से बहुत बेअसर तरीक़े से shield करता है।
तो हर boarding पर, बढ़ता nuclear charge, जैसे कोई conductor अपनी पकड़ कसता है, पूरे electron cloud को थोड़ा और अंदर खींचता है। हर tug छोटा है, पर चौदह elements में जुड़कर steady shrinkage बन जाता है।
एक precision point जो examiners reward करते हैं: ये decrease lanthanoid three plus ions के लिए perfectly regular है, और neutral atoms के लिए सिर्फ़ roughly regular।

Dramatic pay-off periodic table में एक row नीचे दिखता है। Contraction third transition series के लिए expected size increase को लगभग ठीक-ठीक cancel कर देता है, तो zirconium और hafnium one hundred sixty और one hundred fifty nine picometres पर आते हैं, लगभग एक जैसे।

एक naming footnote: lanthanoids को भ्रामक रूप से rare earths कहा गया, हालाँकि ज़्यादातर rare हैं ही नहीं। सिर्फ promethium सचमुच scarce है, जो सिर्फ artificial radioactive element के रूप में मौजूद है।

board_events.text: 1) Third $\approx$ second series: Zr $\approx$ Hf, Nb $\approx$ Ta, Mo $\approx$ W — paired, hard to separate.
2) Hydroxide basicity falls as $\text{Ln}^{3+}$ shrinks: La(OH)$_3$ most basic, Lu(OH)$_3$ least.
3) Density rises across the series — shrinking radius with rising mass.
4) $\Delta_i H_3$ of La, Gd and Lu are abnormally low — they leave $f^0$, $f^7$, $f^{14}$ cores.
One principle threads the colours, moments, oxidation states AND this ionisation pattern.

segments.text: The contraction is not a curiosity to memorise in isolation, it is a cause with four consequences you should be able to recite. The board fans them out from the single shrinking radius.

Consequence one, the big one. The accumulated contraction cancels the expected size jump to the third transition series, so zirconium matches hafnium, niobium matches tantalum, molybdenum matches tungsten. These pairs occur together in nature and are famously difficult to separate.

Consequence two. As the lanthanoid three plus ion shrinks, the metal-to-oxygen-hydrogen bond gains covalent character, so hydroxide basic strength falls. Lanthanum hydroxide is the most basic, lutetium hydroxide the least.
Consequence three. Density rises steadily across the series, because the radius keeps shrinking while the atomic mass keeps rising.
Consequence four is subtle and links straight back to our magnets. The third ionisation enthalpies of lanthanum, gadolinium and lutetium are abnormally low.
The reason: removing that third electron from these particular elements leaves behind the specially stable empty f-zero, half-filled f-seven, and fully-filled f-fourteen cores respectively.

So notice the unity. The same three stability magnets that fix the colours, the magnetic moments and the off-plus-three oxidation states also sculpt this ionisation-enthalpy pattern. One principle threads the entire subtopic.
Contraction अकेले रटने की curiosity नहीं है, ये एक cause है जिसके चार consequences आपको बोलकर याद होने चाहिए। Board इन्हें single shrinking radius से fan out करता है।

Consequence one, सबसे बड़ा। Accumulated contraction third transition series तक expected size jump को cancel कर देता है, तो zirconium hafnium से match करता है, niobium tantalum से, molybdenum tungsten से। ये pairs nature में साथ मिलते हैं और अलग करना बेहद मुश्किल है।

Consequence two। जैसे lanthanoid three plus ion सिकुड़ता है, metal-to-oxygen-hydrogen bond covalent character पाता है, तो hydroxide की basic strength गिरती है। Lanthanum hydroxide सबसे basic है, lutetium hydroxide सबसे कम।
Consequence three। Density series भर steadily बढ़ती है, क्योंकि radius सिकुड़ता रहता है जबकि atomic mass बढ़ता रहता है।
Consequence four subtle है और सीधे हमारे magnets से जुड़ता है। Lanthanum, gadolinium और lutetium की third ionisation enthalpies असामान्य रूप से कम हैं।
वजह: इन ख़ास elements से वो तीसरा electron हटाने पर पीछे क्रमशः specially stable empty f-zero, half-filled f-seven, और fully-filled f-fourteen cores बचते हैं।

तो unity देखो। वही तीन stability magnets जो colours, magnetic moments और off-plus-three oxidation states तय करते हैं, इस ionisation-enthalpy pattern को भी गढ़ते हैं। एक principle पूरे subtopic को जोड़ता है।

board_events.text: Colour arises from $f$–$f$ transitions — an electron promoted between split $4f$ levels.
Because $4f$ is shielded, the absorption bands are sharp and narrow, unlike broad $d$–$d$ bands.
Ions with the same unpaired $4f$ count tend to share a colour.
$f^0$, $f^7$, $f^{14}$ ions are colourless — plus the curious cases Ce$^{3+}$ ($4f^1$) and Yb$^{3+}$ ($4f^{13}$).
So a colour MCQ reduces to counting $4f$ electrons and binning the three magic values.

segments.text: Colour is a reliable source of quick marks here, and it follows a clean rule with one charming set of exceptions.
The board sorts the ions: the three magic counts are colourless, everything in between is coloured.
The colours arise from f-to-f transitions, an electron promoted between the split four f levels when it absorbs a particular wavelength of visible light.

Now a lovely contrast with the transition metals. Because the four f orbitals are shielded deep inside, these absorption bands are characteristically sharp and narrow, quite unlike the broad d-to-d bands of the transition-metal ions.
A handy pattern: lanthanoid ions with the same number of unpaired four f electrons tend to share a colour.

The core rule for MCQs: the f-zero, f-seven and f-fourteen ions are colourless. And there are two famously hard-to-explain extra exceptions, cerium three plus, which is four f one, and ytterbium three plus, which is four f thirteen, are also colourless.
So any colour question reduces to a quick count. Work out the four f electron count, bin the three magic values as colourless, and whatever is left in between is your coloured ion.
Colour यहाँ quick marks का भरोसेमंद source है, और ये एक clean rule follow करता है, एक प्यारे exceptions के set के साथ।
Board ions को sort करता है: तीन magic counts colourless हैं, बीच का सब coloured।
Colours f-to-f transitions से आते हैं, एक electron split four f levels के बीच promote होता है जब वो visible light की एक ख़ास wavelength absorb करता है।

अब transition metals से एक प्यारा contrast। क्योंकि four f orbitals गहरे अंदर shielded हैं, ये absorption bands characteristically sharp और narrow होते हैं, transition-metal ions के broad d-to-d bands से काफ़ी अलग।
एक handy pattern: समान संख्या में unpaired four f electrons वाले lanthanoid ions अक्सर एक जैसा colour रखते हैं।

MCQs के लिए core rule: f-zero, f-seven और f-fourteen ions colourless हैं। और दो मशहूर मुश्किल-से-समझाने वाले extra exceptions हैं, cerium three plus, जो four f one है, और ytterbium three plus, जो four f thirteen है, भी colourless हैं।
तो कोई भी colour question एक quick count में सिमट जाता है। Four f electron count निकालो, तीन magic values को colourless bin करो, और बीच में जो बचे वही आपका coloured ion है।

board_events.text: When plus three is not the whole story
Ask: can losing or gaining one electron from the $+3$ ion reach $f^0$, $f^7$ or $f^{14}$?

board_events.text: $+4$ oxidising states: Ce$^{4+}$ reaches $f^0$; Tb$^{4+}$ reaches $f^7$.
$+2$ reducing states: Eu$^{2+}$ reaches $f^7$; Yb$^{2+}$ reaches $f^{14}$; Sm behaves like Eu.
Rule: states above $+3$ oxidise, below $+3$ reduce — both relax back toward $+3$.

segments.text: We keep saying plus three dominates, and it does, but it is a strong rule, not an absolute one. The exceptions appear in exactly one situation, and there is a single question that predicts them.
Ask this: can the ion, by losing or gaining just one electron from the plus three state, land on a stable f-zero, f-seven or f-fourteen? If yes, that off-plus-three state will appear.
The board places these states on a number line, each with an arrow relaxing back toward plus three.

Take the strongest case on the board. Cerium four plus reaches the empty f-zero, and it is a powerful oxidant, with a standard potential of plus one point seven four volts, eager to fall back to cerium three plus.
So the plus four, oxidising states are those reaching a magic config: cerium four plus to f-zero, and terbium four plus to f-seven.
The plus two, reducing states are the mirror image, reaching a magic config from below: europium two plus to f-seven, ytterbium two plus to f-fourteen, and samarium behaves much like europium.
The unifying rule is clean. Any state above plus three is an oxidiser, any state below plus three is a reducer, and both are simply relaxing back toward the dominant plus three from opposite sides.
हम बार-बार कहते हैं plus three dominate करता है, और करता है, पर ये strong rule है, absolute नहीं। Exceptions ठीक एक situation में आते हैं, और एक ही question इन्हें predict कर देता है।
ये पूछो: क्या ion, plus three state से सिर्फ एक electron खोकर या पाकर, किसी stable f-zero, f-seven या f-fourteen पर आ सकता है? अगर हाँ, तो वो off-plus-three state दिखेगा।
Board इन states को एक number line पर रखता है, हर एक के साथ एक arrow जो plus three की ओर लौटता है।
Board का सबसे strong case लो। Cerium four plus empty f-zero तक पहुँचता है, और ये powerful oxidant है, standard potential plus one point seven four volts, cerium three plus पर वापस गिरने को बेताब।
तो plus four, oxidising states वो हैं जो किसी magic config तक पहुँचते हैं: cerium four plus को f-zero, और terbium four plus को f-seven।
Plus two, reducing states इसका mirror image हैं, नीचे से magic config तक पहुँचते: europium two plus को f-seven, ytterbium two plus को f-fourteen, और samarium काफ़ी हद तक europium जैसा behave करता है।
Unifying rule साफ़ है। Plus three से ऊपर कोई भी state oxidiser है, plus three से नीचे कोई भी state reducer, और दोनों बस opposite sides से dominant plus three की ओर लौट रहे हैं।

board_events.text: Strongly negative $E^{\circ}$ → highly electropositive, reactive metals and strong reducing agents.
With water/dilute acids give H$_2$; heated in O$_2$ give Ln$_2$O$_3$; Ln(OH)$_3$ are strongly basic.
They tarnish in moist air, so they are almost always handled and used as alloys.
Uses: mischmetall (~$95\%$ Ln + ~$5\%$ Fe) for flints/bullets; Ln oxides as phosphors and cracking catalysts.

segments.text: Turn now from ions to the metals themselves, their reactivity, their electrode potential, and where we actually use them.
The board summarises their characteristic reactions around a central lanthanoid metal.
The key number is the electrode potential: lanthanoid three plus over lanthanoid sits around minus two point two to minus two point four volts.

That strongly negative value means these are highly electropositive, reactive metals and strong reducing agents. The earliest members are about as reactive as calcium, tempering to aluminium-like as the series proceeds.

Concretely: with water and dilute acids they liberate hydrogen, forming the three plus ion; heated in oxygen they give the sesquioxides, lanthanoid two o three; and the corresponding hydroxides are definite, strongly basic compounds. They also react with hydrogen, carbon, nitrogen, sulphur and the halogens to give hydrides, carbides, nitrides, sulphides and trihalides.
One practical consequence: the metals tarnish readily in moist air, which is why they are almost always handled and deployed as alloys rather than in the pure state.

And the uses follow from that. Mischmetall, about ninety five percent lanthanoid metal with about five percent iron, goes into lighter flints and tracer bullets; mixed lanthanoid oxides catalyse petroleum cracking; lanthanum oxide polishes optical glass, ceric sulphate is a volumetric oxidant, and several lanthanoid oxides serve as phosphors in television and X-ray screens.
अब ions से metals की ओर चलें, इनकी reactivity, electrode potential, और हम इन्हें असल में कहाँ use करते हैं।
Board एक central lanthanoid metal के इर्द-गिर्द इनकी characteristic reactions summarise करता है।
Key number है electrode potential: lanthanoid three plus over lanthanoid लगभग minus two point two से minus two point four volts पर है।

वो strongly negative value मतलब ये highly electropositive, reactive metals और strong reducing agents हैं। शुरुआती members लगभग calcium जितने reactive हैं, series आगे बढ़ने पर aluminium जैसे होते जाते हैं।

साफ़-साफ़: water और dilute acids के साथ ये hydrogen छोड़ते हैं, three plus ion बनाते; oxygen में गरम करने पर sesquioxides देते हैं, lanthanoid two o three; और उनके hydroxides definite, strongly basic compounds हैं। ये hydrogen, carbon, nitrogen, sulphur और halogens से भी react करके hydrides, carbides, nitrides, sulphides और trihalides देते हैं।
एक practical consequence: metals नम हवा में जल्दी tarnish होते हैं, यही वजह है कि इन्हें लगभग हमेशा pure state के बजाय alloys के रूप में handle और deploy किया जाता है।

और uses उसी से निकलते हैं। Mischmetall, लगभग ninety five percent lanthanoid metal और करीब five percent iron, lighter flints और tracer bullets में जाता है; mixed lanthanoid oxides petroleum cracking को catalyse करते हैं; lanthanum oxide optical glass polish करता है, ceric sulphate एक volumetric oxidant है, और कई lanthanoid oxides television और X-ray screens में phosphors का काम करते हैं।

board_events.text: Shallow $5f$ opens a wide range of states

board_events.caption: Max OS climbs Th to Np, then falls back

<text x="240" y="200" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle">loosely-held 5f early → high states; 5f sinks & becomes core-like → back to +3</text>

board_events.text: $5f$ is less buried than $4f$, so $5f$ electrons can take part in bonding.
$5f$, $6d$ and $7s$ are of comparable energy — electrons from all three are removable.
Early actinoids climb: Th($+4$) $\rightarrow$ Pa($+5$) $\rightarrow$ U($+6$) $\rightarrow$ Np($+7$).
Later, rising charge sinks the $5f$ (a steeper contraction) — the metals fall back to $+3$.
One master variable: how strongly the $5f$ electrons are held.

segments.text: The actinoids are the f-block's wilder cousins, and the reason is one structural difference from the lanthanoids.
The board charts their signature behaviour: the maximum oxidation state climbs and then falls.
The root cause: the five f orbitals are less deeply buried than the lanthanoids' four f, so five f electrons can actually take part in bonding.

More precisely, the five f, six d and seven s levels are all of comparable energy, so electrons from all three sub-levels can be removed with similar ease, opening many oxidation states, from plus three all the way up to plus seven.
Early in the series the five f electrons are only loosely bound, so the maximum state climbs steadily: thorium plus four, protactinium plus five, uranium plus six, neptunium plus seven.

Then it reverses. As atomic number rises further, the increasing nuclear charge pulls the five f electrons progressively inward, an actinoid contraction that is even steeper than the lanthanoid one, because five f shields still more poorly. Once the five f electrons sink and become core-like, they can no longer be removed, so the later actinoids fall back to a lanthanoid-like plus three.
So one master variable runs the whole picture: how strongly the five f electrons are held. Loosely held early gives high, variable states; tightly held late gives plus three only.
Actinoids f-block के wilder cousins हैं, और वजह lanthanoids से एक structural फ़र्क़ है।
Board इनका signature behaviour chart करता है: maximum oxidation state चढ़ता है फिर गिरता है।
मूल वजह: five f orbitals lanthanoids के four f जितने गहरे buried नहीं हैं, तो five f electrons सचमुच bonding में हिस्सा ले सकते हैं।
ज़्यादा सटीक, five f, six d और seven s levels सब comparable energy के हैं, तो तीनों sub-levels से electrons समान आसानी से हट सकते हैं, कई oxidation states खोलते हुए, plus three से लेकर plus seven तक।
Series की शुरुआत में five f electrons सिर्फ loosely bound हैं, तो maximum state steadily चढ़ता है: thorium plus four, protactinium plus five, uranium plus six, neptunium plus seven।

फिर ये उलट जाता है। जैसे atomic number और बढ़ता है, बढ़ता nuclear charge five f electrons को progressively अंदर खींचता है, एक actinoid contraction जो lanthanoid वाली से भी steeper है, क्योंकि five f और भी poorly shield करता है। जैसे ही five f electrons डूबकर core-like हो जाते हैं, वो हट नहीं सकते, तो बाद के actinoids lanthanoid-जैसे plus three पर लौट आते हैं।
तो एक master variable पूरी picture चलाता है: five f electrons कितनी मज़बूती से पकड़े गए हैं। शुरू में loosely held देता है high, variable states; बाद में tightly held देता है सिर्फ plus three।

board_events.text: Both are inner-transition metals dominated by $+3$ and shaped by an $f$-orbital contraction.
But $4f$ is sealed off (monotonous series), while shallow $5f$ buys variable states and stronger complexes.
Every actinoid is radioactive; most beyond uranium are man-made, in trace amounts.
The abundant members carry the uses: Th bred to $^{233}$U; $^{235}$U the classic fuel; $^{239}$Pu from $^{238}$U.
The loosely held, accessible $5f$ electrons that grant rich chemistry also make the nuclei fission-relevant.

segments.text: Let us put the two series side by side, because this comparison is a standard board three-marker, and then close with how the actinoids behave in practice.

The board is the comparison table you should be able to reproduce: inner orbital, oxidation states, contraction, complexes, radioactivity and magnetism, lanthanoids in one column, actinoids in the other.
Read it as one story. Both are inner-transition metals dominated by the plus three state and shaped by an f-orbital contraction.

But the depth of the f orbitals sets them apart. The lanthanoids' four f orbitals are chemically sealed off, so the series is almost monotonous, fourteen near-twins. The actinoids' five f orbitals lie shallow enough to enter bonding, which buys them variable oxidation states and stronger complexes, though also a steeper contraction.

And the universal burden: every single actinoid is radioactive, and most members beyond uranium are man-made, existing only in trace or nanogram amounts, which makes their chemistry genuinely hard to study.

So the few abundant members carry the applications. Thorium is bred into fissile uranium two three three for reactors; uranium two three five is the classic nuclear fuel, and uranium salts colour glass green; plutonium two three nine, obtained from uranium two three eight, is itself a nuclear fuel.

And here is the elegant through-line to remember. The very same loosely held, accessible five f electrons that grant the actinoids their rich oxidation-state chemistry are what make their nuclei fission-relevant. Chemistry and nuclear behaviour spring from one feature.
दोनों series को side by side रखते हैं, क्योंकि ये comparison एक standard board three-marker है, और फिर actinoids practically कैसे behave करते हैं इससे बंद करते हैं।
Board वो comparison table है जिसे आपको reproduce कर पाना चाहिए: inner orbital, oxidation states, contraction, complexes, radioactivity और magnetism, एक column में lanthanoids, दूसरे में actinoids।
इसे एक कहानी की तरह पढ़ो। दोनों inner-transition metals हैं, plus three state से dominated और एक f-orbital contraction से shaped।

पर f orbitals की depth इन्हें अलग करती है। Lanthanoids के four f orbitals chemically sealed off हैं, तो series लगभग monotonous है, चौदह near-twins। Actinoids के five f orbitals इतने shallow हैं कि bonding में आ जाएँ, जो इन्हें variable oxidation states और stronger complexes देता है, हालाँकि एक steeper contraction भी।
और universal बोझ: हर एक actinoid radioactive है, और uranium से आगे के ज़्यादातर members man-made हैं, सिर्फ trace या nanogram मात्रा में, जो इनकी chemistry पढ़ना सचमुच मुश्किल बनाता है।

तो कुछ ही abundant members applications उठाते हैं। Thorium को reactors के लिए fissile uranium two three three में breed किया जाता है; uranium two three five classic nuclear fuel है, और uranium salts glass को green रंगते हैं; plutonium two three nine, uranium two three eight से मिला, ख़ुद nuclear fuel है।

और ये रही याद रखने लायक elegant through-line। वही loosely held, accessible five f electrons जो actinoids को rich oxidation-state chemistry देते हैं, वही इनके nuclei को fission-relevant बनाते हैं। Chemistry और nuclear behaviour एक ही feature से निकलते हैं।

board_events.text: The $4f$ orbitals are so shielded that orbital angular momentum is not quenched.
Spin–orbit coupling matters, so the moment must include the orbital term via $J$.
La$^{3+}$ ($4f^0$) and Lu$^{3+}$ ($4f^{14}$) are diamagnetic; all other Ln$^{3+}$ are paramagnetic.

segments.text: This subtopic has one quantitative formula, and the exam point is knowing when the familiar one fails. The board contrasts the two side by side.
For d-block ions we happily used the spin-only expression, mu-s equals the square root of n times n-plus-two, in Bohr magnetons, and it worked because the orbital contribution was quenched.
For lanthanoid three plus ions it does not work. Instead the observed moment follows mu equals g times the square root of J times J-plus-one, the Landé, or total-angular-momentum, expression.
Why the change? The four f orbitals are so well shielded, tucked deep inside, that their orbital angular momentum is not quenched the way the d-block's is.
Because the orbital motion survives, spin-orbit coupling matters, and the magnetic moment must include the orbital term through the total angular momentum J, not spin alone.

The two clean end-cases you should state instantly: lanthanum three plus, four f zero, and lutetium three plus, four f fourteen, are diamagnetic, having no unpaired electrons. Every other lanthanoid three plus is paramagnetic.

One neat caveat worth a mark: gadolinium three plus, four f seven, has orbital angular momentum L equal to zero, so there the spin-only and the J-formula happen to coincide near seven point nine Bohr magnetons. For most other lanthanoids, though, the two differ markedly.
इस subtopic में एक quantitative formula है, और exam point ये जानना है कि familiar वाला कब fail होता है। Board दोनों को side by side contrast करता है।
d-block ions के लिए हमने ख़ुशी से spin-only expression use किया, mu-s equals square root of n times n-plus-two, Bohr magnetons में, और ये काम करता था क्योंकि orbital contribution quenched था।
Lanthanoid three plus ions के लिए ये काम नहीं करता। बल्कि observed moment follow करता है mu equals g times square root of J times J-plus-one, Landé, यानी total-angular-momentum, expression।
बदलाव क्यों? Four f orbitals इतने well shielded हैं, गहरे अंदर छिपे, कि इनका orbital angular momentum d-block की तरह quenched नहीं होता।
क्योंकि orbital motion बचा रहता है, spin-orbit coupling मायने रखता है, और magnetic moment को orbital term total angular momentum J के ज़रिए शामिल करना पड़ता है, सिर्फ spin नहीं।

दो clean end-cases जो तुरंत बोलने चाहिए: lanthanum three plus, four f zero, और lutetium three plus, four f fourteen, diamagnetic हैं, कोई unpaired electrons नहीं। बाक़ी हर lanthanoid three plus paramagnetic है।

एक neat caveat जो एक mark दिला सकता है: gadolinium three plus, four f seven, का orbital angular momentum L zero के बराबर है, तो वहाँ spin-only और J-formula संयोग से seven point nine Bohr magnetons के पास मिल जाते हैं। पर ज़्यादातर दूसरे lanthanoids के लिए दोनों काफ़ी अलग होते हैं।

board_events.text: The half-filled $4f^7$ is reached early and is extra-stable.
Removing the two $6s$ electrons gives a stable half-filled $f^7$ ion, so Eu shows $+2$.
Eu$^{2+}$ resists losing an $f$ electron → it is a reducing agent, slowly $\rightarrow$ Eu$^{3+}$.

segments.text: Let us apply the stability-magnet idea to a classic board question on europium, atomic number sixty three.
The board shows why europium is stable at f-seven both as the atom and as the two plus ion.
First the configuration. Europium is xenon core, four f seven, six s two. The half-filled four f seven is reached early in the series and is extra-stable.
That half-filled seven is the whole reason for what follows.
Now remove the two six s electrons to form the two plus ion. Europium two plus is xenon core, four f seven, still that stable half-filled configuration.
So europium commonly shows plus two in addition to the characteristic plus three, precisely because the plus two ion lands on the stable f-seven.

And here is the behaviour to state for the mark. Because reverting to plus three would mean losing an electron from that stable f-seven, europium two plus resists it and instead acts as a reducing agent, slowly changing to europium three plus over time.
Stability-magnet idea को europium पर एक classic board question में लगाते हैं, atomic number sixty three।
Board दिखाता है europium f-seven पर क्यों stable है, atom के रूप में भी और two plus ion के रूप में भी।
पहले configuration। Europium xenon core, four f seven, six s two है। Half-filled four f seven series में जल्दी पहुँच जाता है और extra-stable है।
वो half-filled seven ही आगे जो होता है उसकी पूरी वजह है।
अब two plus ion बनाने के लिए दो six s electrons हटाओ। Europium two plus xenon core, four f seven है, अब भी वही stable half-filled configuration।
तो europium characteristic plus three के अलावा आम तौर पर plus two भी दिखाता है, ठीक इसलिए कि plus two ion stable f-seven पर आता है।

और ये रहा वो behaviour जो mark के लिए बताना है। क्योंकि plus three पर लौटने का मतलब उस stable f-seven से एक electron खोना होगा, europium two plus इसका विरोध करता है और बजाय इसके reducing agent की तरह काम करता है, धीरे-धीरे समय के साथ europium three plus में बदलता है।

board_events.text: La$^{3+}$ is $4f^0$, Gd$^{3+}$ is $4f^7$, Lu$^{3+}$ is $4f^{14}$ — all three colourless.
Nd$^{3+}$ is $4f^3$ — partly filled, therefore coloured (lilac).
Answer: Nd$^{3+}$. Eliminate every $f^0$, $f^7$, $f^{14}$ ion first — only the in-between survives.
No computation needed — this is a five-second elimination once the counts are habit.

segments.text: This N E E T speed trap tests the colour rule directly, and it should take you about five seconds with no real computation. Which of lanthanum, gadolinium, neodymium and lutetium three plus is coloured?
The fast way: colour needs a partly filled four f subshell, so simply tag each ion by its four f electron count.
The board bins them visually, the magic values greyed out as colourless.
Lanthanum three plus is four f zero, gadolinium three plus is four f seven, and lutetium three plus is four f fourteen. All three are the magic configs, so all three are colourless.
Neodymium three plus is four f three, a partly filled subshell, and is therefore coloured, a characteristic lilac.

So the answer is neodymium three plus. The speed rule is to eliminate every f-zero, f-seven and f-fourteen ion on sight, that is lanthanum, gadolinium and lutetium, and only the in-between one survives.
Notice you never computed anything. Once the three magic counts are habit, these questions collapse into a five-second elimination, which is exactly the tempo N E E T rewards.
ये N E E T speed trap colour rule को सीधे test करता है, और बिना असली computation के आपको लगभग पाँच सेकंड लेने चाहिए। Lanthanum, gadolinium, neodymium और lutetium three plus में से कौन coloured है?
Fast way: colour को partly filled four f subshell चाहिए, तो बस हर ion को उसके four f electron count से tag करो।
Board इन्हें visually bin करता है, magic values colourless के रूप में greyed out।
Lanthanum three plus four f zero है, gadolinium three plus four f seven, और lutetium three plus four f fourteen। तीनों magic configs हैं, तो तीनों colourless।
Neodymium three plus four f three है, एक partly filled subshell, और इसलिए coloured, एक characteristic lilac।
तो answer है neodymium three plus। Speed rule ये है कि हर f-zero, f-seven और f-fourteen ion को देखते ही eliminate कर दो, यानी lanthanum, gadolinium और lutetium, और सिर्फ बीच वाला बचता है।
ध्यान दो आपने कुछ compute किया ही नहीं। जब तीन magic counts आदत बन जाते हैं, ये questions पाँच-सेकंड elimination में सिमट जाते हैं, ठीक वो tempo जो N E E T reward करता है।

board_events.text: La$^{3+}$ is $4f^0$ → no unpaired electrons → diamagnetic.
Lu$^{3+}$ is $4f^{14}$ → fully filled → diamagnetic.
Gd$^{3+}$ is $4f^7$ → seven unpaired electrons → most strongly paramagnetic.
Spin-only fails: unquenched $4f$ orbital momentum forces the $J$-based moment.

segments.text: This J E E Main question checks both the magnetism rule and the reason the spin-only formula cannot be trusted for lanthanoids. Classify lanthanum, gadolinium and lutetium three plus.
The board shows the unpaired counts as bars: zero, seven, zero.
Lanthanum three plus is four f zero, with no unpaired electrons at all, so it is diamagnetic.
Lutetium three plus is four f fourteen, a completely filled subshell, so it too is diamagnetic.
Gadolinium three plus, by contrast, is four f seven, with seven unpaired electrons, making it the most strongly paramagnetic of the three by a wide margin.
Now the conceptual half of the question, why we cannot just use spin-only here. The moment must be written with the J-based Landé formula, and in general it does not equal the spin-only value.

The reason: for lanthanoid three plus ions the deeply shielded four f orbitals retain unquenched orbital angular momentum, so spin-orbit coupling forces us to include the orbital term through J. Gadolinium three plus is a special case whose half-filled f-seven has L equal to zero, so there the two formulas coincide near seven point nine Bohr magnetons, but that is the exception, not the rule.
ये J E E Main question magnetism rule और वो वजह दोनों check करता है कि lanthanoids के लिए spin-only formula पर भरोसा क्यों नहीं। Lanthanum, gadolinium और lutetium three plus को classify करो।
Board unpaired counts को bars के रूप में दिखाता है: zero, seven, zero।
Lanthanum three plus four f zero है, बिलकुल कोई unpaired electrons नहीं, तो ये diamagnetic है।
Lutetium three plus four f fourteen है, एक completely filled subshell, तो ये भी diamagnetic है।
Gadolinium three plus, इसके उलट, four f seven है, सात unpaired electrons के साथ, जो इसे तीनों में काफ़ी अंतर से सबसे strongly paramagnetic बनाता है।
अब question का conceptual आधा, कि यहाँ हम सिर्फ spin-only क्यों नहीं use कर सकते। Moment को J-based Landé formula से लिखना पड़ता है, और आम तौर पर ये spin-only value के बराबर नहीं होता।

वजह: lanthanoid three plus ions के लिए deeply shielded four f orbitals unquenched orbital angular momentum रखते हैं, तो spin-orbit coupling हमें orbital term J के ज़रिए शामिल करने पर मजबूर करता है। Gadolinium three plus एक special case है जिसके half-filled f-seven का L zero के बराबर है, तो वहाँ दोनों formulas seven point nine Bohr magnetons के पास मिल जाते हैं, पर वो exception है, rule नहीं।

sections.title: Worked example: actinoid oxidation-state range [JEE Advanced]

board_events.text: Why actinoids span more states, and rise then fall

board_events.caption: Comparable 5f/6d/7s energies open the range

<rect x="30" y="42" width="410" height="44" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#1e293b"/>
<text x="235" y="60" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">5f, 6d, 7s of comparable energy & 5f less buried</text>
<text x="235" y="78" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">→ electrons from all three can be removed with similar ease</text>
<rect x="30" y="98" width="410" height="44" fill="#fef3c7" stroke="#1e293b"/>
<text x="235" y="116" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">early (Th→Np): loosely held 5f → max state climbs to +7</text>
<text x="235" y="134" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">later: rising charge sinks 5f (steeper contraction) → back to +3</text>
<text x="235" y="165" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle">one variable: how strongly the 5f electrons are held</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: Wider range: $5f$, $6d$, $7s$ are close in energy, so many electrons are removable.
Lanthanoid $4f$ is energetically isolated — only the three outer electrons are accessible ($+3$).
Early rise: loosely bound $5f$ climb Th$(+4)$ to Np$(+7)$.
Later fall: rising charge sinks $5f$ to core-like → high states impossible, back to $+3$.
One through-line: how strongly the $5f$ electrons are held decides everything.

segments.text: This J E E Advanced question asks two things at once: why actinoids show a far wider oxidation-state range than lanthanoids, and why the maximum state rises across the early actinoids then falls. Both answers share one variable.
The board frames the energetics that open the range.

The wider range comes from energetics. In the actinoids the five f, six d and seven s levels are all of comparable energy, and the five f orbitals are less buried, so electrons from all three can be removed with similar ease, opening states from plus three up to plus seven.

Contrast the lanthanoids, where the four f orbitals lie deep below the valence level, energetically isolated, so only the three outermost electrons are chemically accessible, which is why they are almost exclusively plus three.

Now the rise. Early in the actinoid series, thorium through neptunium, the five f electrons are only loosely bound and readily participate, so the maximum state climbs: thorium plus four, protactinium plus five, uranium plus six, neptunium plus seven.

Then the fall. As atomic number increases further, the rising nuclear charge pulls the five f electrons progressively inward, the actinoid contraction, steeper than the lanthanoid one. Once the five f electrons sink and become core-like, they can no longer be removed for high oxidation states, so the later actinoids fall back to the stable plus three.

So state the synthesis explicitly: the single variable, how strongly the five f electrons are held, explains both facts. Loosely held early gives high, variable states; tightly held late gives plus three only.

ये J E E Advanced question एक साथ दो चीज़ें पूछता है: actinoids lanthanoids से कहीं wider oxidation-state range क्यों दिखाते हैं, और early actinoids में maximum state क्यों चढ़ता फिर गिरता है। दोनों जवाब एक variable साझा करते हैं।
Board वो energetics frame करता है जो range खोलती है।

Wider range energetics से आती है। Actinoids में five f, six d और seven s levels सब comparable energy के हैं, और five f orbitals कम buried हैं, तो तीनों से electrons समान आसानी से हट सकते हैं, plus three से plus seven तक states खोलते हुए।

Lanthanoids से contrast करो, जहाँ four f orbitals valence level से काफ़ी नीचे हैं, energetically isolated, तो सिर्फ तीन outermost electrons chemically accessible हैं, यही वजह है कि वो लगभग सिर्फ plus three हैं।

अब rise। Actinoid series की शुरुआत में, thorium से neptunium तक, five f electrons सिर्फ loosely bound हैं और आसानी से हिस्सा लेते हैं, तो maximum state चढ़ता है: thorium plus four, protactinium plus five, uranium plus six, neptunium plus seven।

फिर fall। जैसे atomic number और बढ़ता है, बढ़ता nuclear charge five f electrons को progressively अंदर खींचता है, actinoid contraction, lanthanoid से steeper। जैसे ही five f electrons डूबकर core-like हो जाते हैं, वो high oxidation states के लिए हट नहीं सकते, तो बाद के actinoids stable plus three पर लौट आते हैं।

तो synthesis साफ़ बोलो: एक variable, five f electrons कितनी मज़बूती से पकड़े गए, दोनों facts समझा देता है। शुरू में loosely held देता है high, variable states; बाद में tightly held देता है सिर्फ plus three।

board_events.text: Four traps, and one idea that beats them all
Trap 1: using spin-only for lanthanoids. Their unquenched orbital momentum needs $\mu=g\sqrt{J(J+1)}$.
Trap 2: stating the contraction cause backwards — it is POOR $4f$ shielding, not appreciable.
Trap 3: assuming every Ln ion is $+3$, coloured and paramagnetic — the magic configs break all three.
Trap 4: forgetting La and Ac are $d$-block — their differentiating electron is in $d$, not $f$.

board_events.text: Mnemonic: 'LA-GD-LU are colourless and diamagnetic' ($f^0$, $f^7$, $f^{14}$).

segments.text: Let us close the f-block with the four traps that cost marks, and the single idea that lets you sidestep most of them.

Trap one, the most common numerical error. Do not use the spin-only formula for lanthanoids; it works for d-block ions but not for lanthanoid three plus, whose unquenched orbital momentum requires the J-based Landé expression.

Trap two, a wording trap in reasoning questions. State the contraction's cause the right way round: it is the poor, imperfect shielding by four f electrons, not appreciable shielding. The poor shielding is the whole point.

Trap three, over-generalising. Do not assume every lanthanoid ion is plus three, coloured and paramagnetic. The magic configurations break all three of those at once, giving colourless, diamagnetic, off-plus-three species.

Trap four, a classification slip. Do not forget that lanthanum and actinium are d-block elements; they are grouped with the f-block only by resemblance, since their differentiating electron sits in d, not f.
The reference card on the board is your master tool.

Build everything on the f-zero, f-seven, f-fourteen stability magnets. They tell you which ions are colourless and diamagnetic, which off-plus-three states form, and whether each off-state is oxidising or reducing. One idea, three exam answers. And lock the mnemonic: L-A, G-D, L-U are colourless and diamagnetic, the f-zero, f-seven and f-fourteen ions.
f-block को चार traps के साथ बंद करते हैं जो marks खाते हैं, और वो एक idea जो इनमें से ज़्यादातर से बचा देता है।

Trap one, सबसे common numerical error। Lanthanoids के लिए spin-only formula मत use करो; ये d-block ions के लिए काम करता है पर lanthanoid three plus के लिए नहीं, जिसका unquenched orbital momentum J-based Landé expression माँगता है।

Trap two, reasoning questions में एक wording trap। Contraction की वजह सही तरीक़े से बोलो: ये four f electrons की poor, imperfect shielding है, appreciable shielding नहीं। Poor shielding ही पूरी बात है।

Trap three, over-generalise करना। ये मत मान लो कि हर lanthanoid ion plus three, coloured और paramagnetic है। Magic configurations तीनों को एक साथ तोड़ देती हैं, colourless, diamagnetic, off-plus-three species देती हैं।

Trap four, एक classification की चूक। ये मत भूलो कि lanthanum और actinium d-block elements हैं; इन्हें f-block के साथ सिर्फ resemblance से रखा गया है, क्योंकि इनका differentiating electron d में है, f में नहीं।
Board का reference card आपका master tool है।

सब कुछ f-zero, f-seven, f-fourteen stability magnets पर बनाओ। ये बताते हैं कौन-से ions colourless और diamagnetic हैं, कौन-सी off-plus-three states बनती हैं, और हर off-state oxidising है या reducing। एक idea, तीन exam answers। और mnemonic lock करो: L-A, G-D, L-U colourless और diamagnetic हैं, वो f-zero, f-seven और f-fourteen ions।

board_events.text: Thread 1: $E^{\circ}$ is one number that summarises reactivity — negative means reactive.
A positive value (copper) means the metal clings to its electrons — it is 'noble'.
Thread 2: the M$^{3+}$/M$^{2+}$ couple is decided by the config the M$^{3+}$ lands on.
Thread 3: $3d\rightarrow4d\rightarrow5d$ should grow, but the contraction flattens $4d$→$5d$ — $2$nd $\approx 3$rd.
These are reference-desk facts — standard, aqueous conditions, read as trends not smooth curves.

segments.text: The three earlier subtopics built the why of the transition metals. This capstone is the reference desk: the hard numbers and side-by-side comparisons you must have at your fingertips to actually answer exam questions.
Three threads tie it together, laid out on the board.

Thread one: a standard electrode potential is a single number that summarises reactivity. A very negative electrode potential for the metal-two-plus over metal couple means the metal would rather stay oxidised, so it is reactive and a good reducing agent. Think of it as a batting average for electron-hunger.
A positive value, as for copper, means the opposite: the metal clings to its electrons and is described as noble.

Thread two: the metal-three-plus over metal-two-plus couple answers a different question, how willing an existing two-plus ion is to give up one more electron. The answer is dictated entirely by the configuration the resulting three-plus ion lands on.

Thread three: going down a group, from three d to four d to five d, you would expect steady size growth, but the lanthanoid contraction flattens the four-d-to-five-d step, so the second and third series end up uncannily alike while the first stands apart.

One caveat before the tables: these are reference-desk facts for standard, aqueous conditions. The values carry irregularities, so read them as trends, not smooth curves, and remember reactivity here means electropositive, redox reactivity, not kinetic rate.
पिछले तीन subtopics ने transition metals का why बनाया। ये capstone reference desk है: वो hard numbers और side-by-side comparisons जो exam questions जवाब देने के लिए उँगलियों पर होने चाहिए।
तीन threads इसे जोड़ते हैं, board पर रखे।

Thread one: standard electrode potential एक single number है जो reactivity summarise करता है। Metal-two-plus over metal couple के लिए बहुत negative electrode potential मतलब metal oxidised ही रहना पसंद करता है, तो ये reactive और अच्छा reducing agent है। इसे electron-hunger का batting average समझो।
Positive value, जैसे copper के लिए, उल्टा मतलब: metal अपने electrons से चिपका रहता है और noble कहलाता है।

Thread two: metal-three-plus over metal-two-plus couple एक अलग सवाल का जवाब देता है, कि मौजूद two-plus ion एक और electron देने को कितना तैयार है। जवाब पूरी तरह इस पर निर्भर है कि बनने वाला three-plus ion किस configuration पर आता है।

Thread three: group में नीचे जाते, three d से four d से five d, आप steady size growth की उम्मीद करेंगे, पर lanthanoid contraction four-d-to-five-d step को flatten कर देता है, तो दूसरी और तीसरी series हैरतअंगेज़ तरीक़े से एक जैसी हो जाती हैं जबकि पहली अलग खड़ी रहती है।

Tables से पहले एक caveat: ये standard, aqueous conditions के reference-desk facts हैं। Values में irregularities होती हैं, तो इन्हें trends की तरह पढ़ो, smooth curves की तरह नहीं, और याद रखो यहाँ reactivity मतलब electropositive, redox reactivity, kinetic rate नहीं।

board_events.text: Mostly negative — these metals lie above hydrogen and displace H$_2$ from dilute acids.
Copper alone is positive ($+0.34$ V, noble); Mn and Zn are more negative than the smooth trend.
The Mn/Zn dips reflect the stability of the resulting Mn$^{2+}$ ($d^5$) and Zn$^{2+}$ ($d^{10}$).
A favourable $E^{\circ}$ appears when low $\Delta_a H+\Delta_i H$ are well repaid by a large hydration energy.

segments.text: Now the first big table, and this is the full home of the electrode-potential reasoning we only touched lightly back in the trends subtopic.

The starting principle: for a metal going to its aqueous two-plus ion, the overall standard potential is fixed by the sum of three energy terms, the enthalpy of atomisation, the ionisation enthalpy, and the hydration enthalpy of the ion.
The board plots the metal-two-plus over metal values across the three d series.
Read the shape. The values are mostly negative, which means these metals lie above hydrogen in the activity order and displace hydrogen gas from dilute acids.

Two features stand out. Copper alone is positive, at plus zero point three four volts, so it is noble and cannot liberate hydrogen. And manganese and zinc are more negative than the smooth trend would predict.

Those manganese and zinc dips are the exam point. They reflect the extra stability of the resulting ions, manganese two plus is a half-filled d-five, and zinc two plus is a filled d-ten, which makes forming those ions unusually favourable.

So the unifying reading: a favourable, more negative potential appears when low atomisation and ionisation energies are well repaid by a large, exothermic hydration energy. When they are not, as with copper, the metal prefers to stay a metal.
अब पहली बड़ी table, और यही electrode-potential reasoning का पूरा घर है जिसे हमने trends subtopic में सिर्फ हल्के से छुआ था।

Starting principle: एक metal के अपने aqueous two-plus ion तक जाने के लिए, overall standard potential तीन energy terms के sum से तय होता है, enthalpy of atomisation, ionisation enthalpy, और ion की hydration enthalpy।
Board metal-two-plus over metal values को three d series भर plot करता है।
Shape पढ़ो। Values ज़्यादातर negative हैं, मतलब ये metals activity order में hydrogen के ऊपर हैं और dilute acids से hydrogen gas displace करते हैं।

दो features उभरते हैं। Copper अकेला positive है, plus zero point three four volts पर, तो ये noble है और hydrogen liberate नहीं कर सकता। और manganese व zinc smooth trend की उम्मीद से ज़्यादा negative हैं।

वो manganese और zinc के dips exam point हैं। ये बनने वाले ions की extra stability दिखाते हैं, manganese two plus half-filled d-five है, और zinc two plus filled d-ten, जो उन ions को बनाना असामान्य रूप से favourable बनाता है।

तो unifying reading: एक favourable, ज़्यादा negative potential तब आता है जब low atomisation और ionisation energies एक large, exothermic hydration energy से अच्छी तरह चुका दी जाएँ। जब नहीं, जैसे copper के साथ, metal, metal ही रहना पसंद करता है।

board_events.text: Cr$^{3+}$/Cr$^{2+}=-0.41$ V (negative): Cr$^{2+}$ is a reducing agent, oxidised to the stable $d^3$.
Fe$^{3+}$/Fe$^{2+}=+0.77$ V (moderate): Fe$^{3+}$ ($d^5$) is comparatively stable, a mild oxidiser.
Mn$^{3+}$/Mn$^{2+}=+1.57$ V: Mn$^{3+}$ falls readily to the stable $d^5$ Mn$^{2+}$ — strong oxidiser.
Co$^{3+}$/Co$^{2+}=+1.97$ V: the highest, driven by the huge hydration enthalpy of small Co$^{3+}$.
The trend is not monotonic — it is sculpted by the stability of the resulting $d^n$ configuration.

segments.text: The second table is the one that decides oxidising versus reducing behaviour, the metal-three-plus over metal-two-plus couple. The trick is not to memorise numbers but to read each couple by the configuration the three-plus ion reaches.
The board shows the values, negative on one side, large positive on the other.

Chromium three plus over chromium two plus is minus zero point four one volts, negative. So chromium two plus is a reducing agent, readily oxidised because chromium three plus is the extra-stable half-filled d-three.
Iron three plus over iron two plus is plus zero point seven seven volts, only moderate. So iron three plus, being d-five, is comparatively stable and acts as just a mild oxidiser.
Manganese three plus over manganese two plus jumps to plus one point five seven volts. Manganese three plus falls readily to the stable d-five manganese two plus, so it is a strong oxidiser.

Cobalt three plus over cobalt two plus is the highest, plus one point nine seven volts. Here the driving force is the exceptionally large hydration enthalpy of the small, highly charged cobalt three plus ion, which powerfully favours its reduction.

So notice the trend is not monotonic with atomic number. It is sculpted by the stability of the resulting d-n configuration, plus the hydration of the highly charged three-plus ion. The very same half-filled and empty-shell logic that runs through colour, magnetism and ionisation enthalpy governs these potentials too.

दूसरी table वही है जो oxidising versus reducing behaviour तय करती है, metal-three-plus over metal-two-plus couple। Trick numbers रटना नहीं, बल्कि हर couple को इस configuration से पढ़ना है जिस पर three-plus ion पहुँचता है।
Board values दिखाता है, एक तरफ negative, दूसरी तरफ large positive।

Chromium three plus over chromium two plus minus zero point four one volts है, negative। तो chromium two plus reducing agent है, आसानी से oxidise होता क्योंकि chromium three plus extra-stable half-filled d-three है।
Iron three plus over iron two plus plus zero point seven seven volts है, सिर्फ moderate। तो iron three plus, d-five होने से, comparatively stable है और सिर्फ mild oxidiser की तरह काम करता है।
Manganese three plus over manganese two plus plus one point five seven volts तक कूदता है। Manganese three plus आसानी से stable d-five manganese two plus पर गिरता है, तो ये strong oxidiser है।

Cobalt three plus over cobalt two plus सबसे ऊँचा है, plus one point nine seven volts। यहाँ driving force छोटे, highly charged cobalt three plus ion की असाधारण रूप से बड़ी hydration enthalpy है, जो इसके reduction को ज़ोरदार favour करती है।

तो ध्यान दो trend atomic number के साथ monotonic नहीं है। ये बनने वाले d-n configuration की stability, और highly charged three-plus ion के hydration से गढ़ा जाता है। वही half-filled और empty-shell logic जो colour, magnetism और ionisation enthalpy में चलता है, इन potentials को भी चलाता है।

board_events.text: Colour is set by the number of unpaired $d$-electrons via $d$–$d$ transitions.
Sc$^{3+}$ ($d^0$) and Zn$^{2+}$ ($d^{10}$) sit at the two ends — both colourless.
In between: Ti$^{3+}$ purple, Cr$^{3+}$ violet, Mn$^{2+}$ pale pink, Fe$^{3+}$ yellow, Cu$^{2+}$ blue.
Same unpaired count often shares a moment: Ti$^{3+}$ and Cu$^{2+}$ both $1.73$; Mn$^{2+}$ and Fe$^{3+}$ both $5.92$.
These are the common aqua ions — a different ligand field can shift the colour.

segments.text: The third reference is colour, and this is a table to memorise cold, because it lets you identify an ion or rule out a distractor instantly.
The board gives the full set: each hydrated three d ion with its configuration, unpaired-electron count, spin-only moment, and characteristic colour.
The organising idea, from the very first subtopic, is that colour is set by the number of unpaired d-electrons through d-to-d transitions.
Anchor the two ends first. Scandium three plus is d-zero and zinc two plus is d-ten, both lacking a partly filled subshell, so both are colourless.
Fill in the middle: titanium three plus is purple, chromium three plus violet, manganese two plus pale pink, iron three plus yellow, copper two plus blue, and so on across the row.

A neat consistency check: ions with the same unpaired count share a spin-only moment. Titanium three plus and copper two plus both have one unpaired electron, so both sit at one point seven three; manganese two plus and iron three plus both have five, so both are five point nine two.

One caveat worth stating: these colours are for the common hydrated aqua ions. The same metal in a different ligand field can look quite different, which is a preview of the coordination-compounds chapter ahead.
तीसरा reference colour है, और ये table cold याद करने लायक है, क्योंकि ये किसी ion को तुरंत पहचानने या distractor को rule out करने देती है।
Board पूरा set देता है: हर hydrated three d ion अपनी configuration, unpaired-electron count, spin-only moment, और characteristic colour के साथ।
Organising idea, बिलकुल पहले subtopic से, ये है कि colour unpaired d-electrons की संख्या से d-to-d transitions के ज़रिए तय होता है।
पहले दोनों सिरे anchor करो। Scandium three plus d-zero है और zinc two plus d-ten, दोनों में partly filled subshell नहीं, तो दोनों colourless हैं।
बीच भरो: titanium three plus purple, chromium three plus violet, manganese two plus pale pink, iron three plus yellow, copper two plus blue, और ऐसे ही row भर।

एक neat consistency check: समान unpaired count वाले ions एक spin-only moment साझा करते हैं। Titanium three plus और copper two plus दोनों में एक unpaired electron, तो दोनों one point seven three पर; manganese two plus और iron three plus दोनों में पाँच, तो दोनों five point nine two।
एक caveat बताना ज़रूरी: ये colours common hydrated aqua ions के लिए हैं। वही metal अलग ligand field में काफ़ी अलग दिख सकता है, जो आगे आने वाले coordination-compounds chapter की झलक है।

sections.title: Reactivity with acids

board_events.text: Who liberates hydrogen, and who needs more

board_events.caption: Reactivity falls Sc to Cu
board_events.svg: <svg font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" viewBox="0 0 480 200" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="480" height="200" fill="#ffffff"/><text x="240" y="22" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">Reactivity with acids falls Sc → Cu</text><rect x="20" y="40" width="440" height="40" fill="#dcfce7" stroke="#1e293b"/><text x="30" y="57" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10">Negative E°(M²⁺/M): dissolve in dilute HCl / H₂SO₄, releasing H₂</text><text x="30" y="73" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10">e.g. Fe + 2 H⁺ → Fe²⁺ + H₂</text><rect x="20" y="90" width="440" height="40" fill="#fee2e2" stroke="#1e293b"/><text x="30" y="107" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10">Cu (positive E°): no H₂ from dilute acid; needs an oxidising acid</text><text x="30" y="123" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10">3 Cu + 8 HNO₃(dil.) → 3 Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2 NO + 4 H₂O</text><rect x="20" y="140" width="440" height="34" fill="#e5e7eb" stroke="#1e293b"/><text x="240" y="161" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle">Pt, Au are the most noble — resist even single mineral acids</text></svg>

board_events.text: Metals with negative $E^{\circ}(\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M})$ dissolve in dilute HCl or H$_2$SO$_4$, releasing H$_2$.
Copper's positive $E^{\circ}$ means no H$_2$ from dilute acid — it needs an oxidising acid.
There the nitrate anion, not H$^+$, does the oxidising.
Pt and Au are the most noble of all — they resist even single mineral acids.

segments.text: Reactivity with acids follows directly from the metal-two-plus over metal potentials, and it broadly decreases from scandium to copper across the row.
The board splits the behaviour into the reactive majority, the copper exception, and the truly noble metals.

Most of the series has a negative electrode potential, so these metals dissolve in dilute non-oxidising acids like hydrochloric or sulphuric, liberating hydrogen. Iron plus two protons gives iron two plus and hydrogen gas.
Copper is the exception. Its positive potential means it will not liberate hydrogen from dilute hydrochloric or sulphuric acid at all. It dissolves only in an oxidising acid such as nitric acid.
The board gives that reaction: three copper plus eight dilute nitric acid give copper nitrate, nitric oxide, and water.
The key insight there is that the nitrate anion, not the hydrogen ion, is doing the oxidising, which is why an ordinary non-oxidising acid fails.
And at the far end sit the very high-melting heavy metals, platinum and gold, the most noble of all, which resist even single mineral acids and need special mixtures to dissolve.
Acids के साथ reactivity सीधे metal-two-plus over metal potentials से निकलती है, और ये मोटे तौर पर scandium से copper तक row भर घटती है।
Board behaviour को तीन में बाँटता है: reactive बहुमत, copper exception, और सचमुच noble metals।

Series का ज़्यादातर हिस्सा negative electrode potential रखता है, तो ये metals dilute non-oxidising acids जैसे hydrochloric या sulphuric में घुलते हैं, hydrogen liberate करते हुए। Iron plus दो protons देते हैं iron two plus और hydrogen gas।
Copper exception है। इसका positive potential मतलब ये dilute hydrochloric या sulphuric acid से hydrogen बिलकुल liberate नहीं करेगा। ये सिर्फ एक oxidising acid जैसे nitric acid में घुलता है।
Board वो reaction देता है: तीन copper plus आठ dilute nitric acid देते हैं copper nitrate, nitric oxide, और water।
वहाँ key insight ये है कि nitrate anion, hydrogen ion नहीं, oxidising कर रहा है, यही वजह है कि एक साधारण non-oxidising acid fail होता है।
और दूसरे छोर पर बहुत high-melting heavy metals हैं, platinum और gold, सबसे noble, जो single mineral acids का भी विरोध करते हैं और घुलने के लिए special mixtures चाहिए।

board_events.text: Oxidation state controls the oxide

board_events.caption: Basic to amphoteric to acidic as OS rises
board_events.svg: <svg font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" viewBox="0 0 480 210" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="480" height="210" fill="#ffffff"/><text x="240" y="22" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">Oxidation state controls oxide character</text><rect x="40" y="45" width="120" height="46" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#1e293b"/><text x="100" y="66" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle">low OS</text><text x="100" y="82" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">MnO: basic</text><rect x="180" y="45" width="120" height="46" fill="#fef3c7" stroke="#1e293b"/><text x="240" y="66" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle">middle OS</text><text x="240" y="82" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">MnO₂: amphoteric</text><rect x="320" y="45" width="120" height="46" fill="#fee2e2" stroke="#1e293b"/><text x="380" y="66" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle">high OS</text><text x="380" y="82" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">Mn₂O₇: acidic</text><text x="160" y="86" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="16">→</text><text x="300" y="86" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="16">→</text><text x="240" y="130" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">highest oxide OS = group number up to Mn:</text><text x="240" y="150" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">Sc₂O₃, TiO₂, V₂O₅, CrO₃, Mn₂O₇</text><text x="240" y="180" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="#b00020">O and F stabilise the highest states: OsO₄ (+8), MnO₄⁻ (+7), CrO₃ (+6)</text></svg>

board_events.text: The highest oxide oxidation state matches the group number up to Mn.
Sc$_2$O$_3$, TiO$_2$, V$_2$O$_5$, CrO$_3$, Mn$_2$O$_7$ — then it falls off thereafter.
Acidic character rises with oxidation state: low basic, middle amphoteric, highest acidic.
Oxygen and fluorine stabilise the highest states: OsO$_4$ ($+8$), MnO$_4^-$ ($+7$), CrO$_3$ ($+6$).
The acidic high-state oxides dissolve in alkali to give oxoanions — chromate, permanganate.

segments.text: Oxides and halides give another clean, rule-governed reference, and the governing variable is again the oxidation state.
The board runs the acidity ladder for manganese, basic to amphoteric to acidic as the state rises.
First fact: the highest oxide oxidation state matches the group number, all the way up to manganese.
So we get scandium two o three, titanium dioxide, vanadium pentoxide, chromium trioxide, and manganese two o seven, and beyond manganese the attainable maximum falls off.

Second fact, the acidity trend within an element: acidic character rises with oxidation state. Low states give basic oxides, intermediate states amphoteric, and the highest states acidic, exactly as manganese runs from basic manganese oxide to amphoteric manganese dioxide to acidic manganese two o seven.

Third, and a favourite exam line: oxygen and fluorine stabilise the highest oxidation states, thanks to their small size, high electronegativity, and ability to form multiple bonds. That is why the very top states appear in oxides and fluorides, osmium tetroxide at plus eight, permanganate at plus seven, chromium trioxide at plus six.
And to close the loop with the second subtopic: those acidic high-state oxides dissolve in alkali to give the oxometallic salts, the chromates and permanganates we studied in detail earlier.
Oxides और halides एक और clean, rule-governed reference देते हैं, और governing variable फिर से oxidation state है।
Board manganese के लिए acidity ladder चलाता है, state बढ़ने पर basic से amphoteric से acidic।
पहला fact: highest oxide oxidation state group number से match करता है, पूरा manganese तक।
तो हमें मिलते हैं scandium two o three, titanium dioxide, vanadium pentoxide, chromium trioxide, और manganese two o seven, और manganese के आगे attainable maximum गिर जाता है।

दूसरा fact, एक element के भीतर acidity trend: acidic character oxidation state के साथ बढ़ता है। Low states basic oxides देते हैं, intermediate amphoteric, और highest states acidic, ठीक जैसे manganese basic manganese oxide से amphoteric manganese dioxide से acidic manganese two o seven तक चलता है।

तीसरा, और एक favourite exam line: oxygen और fluorine highest oxidation states को stabilise करते हैं, अपने small size, high electronegativity, और multiple bonds बनाने की क्षमता के कारण। इसीलिए सबसे top states oxides और fluorides में आते हैं, osmium tetroxide plus eight पर, permanganate plus seven पर, chromium trioxide plus six पर।
और दूसरे subtopic से loop बंद करने के लिए: वो acidic high-state oxides alkali में घुलकर oxometallic salts देते हैं, वही chromates और permanganates जो पहले विस्तार से पढ़े।
